pick.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +0.8%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $20.06 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 114 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-22.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-05) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
stories.excerpt: Company says foreign-made robotic vehicles are crucial to US chip production.
stories.lead:
US chip champion Intel was so confused by the US government ban on foreign-made robots that it requested and received a waiver “out of an abundance of caution.” The tech company wanted to make sure that it could continue using certain robotic vehicles in its US chip fabs.

The uncertainty surrounding the Federal Communications Commission ban on certain foreign-made robots was revealed in the agency’s decision to grant Intel’s waiver request. On October 22, the FCC published its order allowing Intel to continue using the foreign-made robots in US semiconductor manufacturing facilities for a period of one year.

stories.title: An Intro to Threading in Python
stories.excerpt: Learn how to use Python threading to run tasks concurrently, synchronize threads with locks and queues, and avoid race conditions and deadlocks.
stories.lead:
Python threading allows you to have different parts of your program run concurrently and can simplify your design. If you’ve got some experience in Python and want to speed up your program using threads, then this tutorial is for you!

This article assumes you’ve got the Python basics down pat and that you’re using at least version 3.6 to run the examples. If you need a refresher, you can start with the Python Learning Paths and get up to speed.

If you’re not sure if you want to use Python threading, asyncio, or multiprocessing, then you can check out Speed Up Your Python Program With Concurrency.

stories.title: Police arrested 1,314 in French protests, government says
stories.excerpt: It was the second consecutive weekend of unrest in France, which is heading to presidential elections in April and May to choose a successor to Emmanuel Macron, who is reaching his two-term limit.

stories.title: More than 1,300 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
stories.excerpt: Hundreds of thousands took part in demonstrations in France, with protests also taking place in other European countries.
stories.lead:
In the southern port of Marseille, rubbish bins were set ablaze and metal sheets used to block streets. A law enforcement vehicle was seen driving through a burning barricade in France's second-largest city.

Meanwhile, some protesters in dark clothing and face coverings were seen taking boards off a building to build a street barricade in the southern city of Bordeaux.

In Lyon, police used tear gas grenades to disperse a crowd which had reportedly gathered in an area deemed off-limits by the local prefecture.

stories.title: The College of Magic turns ordinary kids into confident, top-hat wearing magicians
stories.excerpt: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.
stories.lead:
Dressed in a sharp black three-piece suit and a dapper yellow bow tie, Lubelo Mthenjana stands alone on a dark stage, taking in the last few seconds of quiet before the curtain opens. He takes a deep breath as his name is announced. Then he opens his arms wide and flashes a bright smile.

"Hello everyone! My name is Lubelo Mthenjana, and I will be performing for you … some magic!"

stories.title: Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe
stories.excerpt: While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.
stories.lead:
MILAN — Thousands of young people marched Saturday through the streets of several Italian cities, including Milan, Rome and Turin, as authorities deployed large numbers of police and soldiers in a largely successful bid to stave off a repeat of the violent clashes and looting that marred similar protests last week.

The demonstration in Milan remained peaceful, but there were brief clashes with police in both Rome and Turin.

In Milan, thousands of young people marched the streets as soldiers were deployed and luxury boutiques were boarded up, but by late afternoon, most shops had opened, Italian media reported.

stories.title: In Arkansas, Democrats see an opening at the edge of the competitive midterms map
stories.excerpt: In a sign of the potentially dire midterm political environment, Republicans have spent millions of dollars playing defense in Arkansas, one of the most conservative states in the country.
stories.lead:
HOPE, Ark. — For Senate candidate Hallie Shoffner, the most important political label she wears isn't that she's a Democrat. Or that she's not a Republican. Instead, it's that she is an Arkansan.

As a lunchtime crowd ate at Tailgater's Burger Company Friday, Shoffner decried what she called a historically unproductive Congress driven by extreme voices in each party and pitched herself to receptive — if skeptical — voters as a candidate who would better serve their needs.

Arkansas is one of the most conservative states in the country, with nearly two out of three voters supporting President Trump in 2024 and Republican Sen. Tom Cotton in 2020.

stories.title: Budget to include £1bn for social and affordable housing
stories.excerpt: The move will take funding for the 10-year programme to more than £40bn.
stories.lead:
More than £1bn for social and affordable housing in England will be provided in the Budget, taking funding for the government's 10-year homes programme past £40bn.

Mayors and regional leaders across England are also expected to get greater powers and funding in Wednesday's announcement - with councils helped to borrow money from the government to invest in house-building through preferential interest rates.

It is hoped the plans will give regional leaders more flexibility and authority over investment decisions.

stories.title: Comeback Falls Short for Men's Water Polo
stories.excerpt: No. 18 Harvard clipped by No. 10 UC Davis, 12-11.
stories.lead:
SAN JOSE, Calif. -- The No. 18 Harvard men's water polo team lost a close top-20 match-up with No. 10 UC Davis, 12-11. at San Jose State in the Julian Fraser Memorial Tournament on Saturday afternoon. The Crimson fell to 10-12 on the season with one game left to play in the tournament before finishing the regular season in the Northeast.

Trailing 12-7 with less than four minutes to play, Harvard charged back with four goals, including two from junior Lukas Peabody and first-year Clay Carrington to trim the deficit to one, but time ran out before the Crimson could find an equalizer. Carrington and junior Dean Strauser tied for the team-lead in goals with four.
